releases.body:
### VS Code deep integration

* Link any project to a generated `.code-workspace` from the wizard, project card
  or Config panel. Linked projects show a badge and an **Open in VS Code** action.
* Two launch modes: host the TUI in VS Code's integrated terminal (seamless
  `@file#lines` selection insertion) or keep the external terminal while VS Code
  follows edits. A per-run override is available from the Run caret.
* Live edit following: the global OpenCode event stream is mapped to a project,
  validated against the project root, debounced and sent to the companion for
  reveal + highlight. Without the companion, linked projects fall back to
  `code --reuse-window --goto`.
* Companion extension (`perun.perun-overseer`): status bar, ticket-authenticated
  loopback WebSocket, selection command (`Ctrl+Alt+P`), terminal open/focus/close,
  and `terminal.processId` binding so Stop/Focus keep working.
* Security: single-use workspace-bound tickets, no long-lived token in a URL,
  fixed message schema, loopback-only endpoints, ignored workspace-level
  `perun.*` settings, path validation, and no silent VS Code install.
* VSIX is built in the release workflow and installed per-user by the Windows
  installer; the dashboard reports a missing/outdated companion.

### Documentation refresh

* `README.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md` now describe the Telegram card grammar,
  coloured buttons, live run drafts and per-chat message scheduling;
  `AGENTS_OPTIMIZATION.md` and the Shared Projects PRD name v0.13.3.

### Telegram bridge: finish the audit follow-ups

* The run path now joins the live-draft thread (up to 1 s) before sending the
  final answer, so an in-flight draft update cannot leave a stale "Working…"
  preview after the reply. Tool events obey the same 1.6 s throttle.
* `setMyCommands` uses `retries=1` at startup, so an outage cannot delay the
  poller by the full retry budget.
* Plain messages from different chats now run concurrently (one run per chat),
  so a long agent run in one chat no longer blocks messages from another. The
  durable queue still delivers per-chat updates in order.
* `format_html()` strips NUL bytes before inserting private placeholders, so
  agent text containing a literal placeholder can no longer corrupt output.

### Harden the Telegram delivery fallbacks

* Only a definite Telegram `400` now triggers the plain-text/degraded-keyboard
  fallback; a timeout or unreachable host no longer causes blind extra sends
  that could duplicate a message the operator already received.
* `api()` returns a non-429 `4xx` immediately instead of retrying it four times,
  so a bad entity falls back to plain text at once rather than after ~14 s.
* `editMessageText`'s "message is not modified" response counts as success, so
  tapping an unchanged card can no longer post a duplicate card.
* The draft Stop handler re-checks that the chat is authorised before cancelling.

### The draft Stop button now reaches the bridge

* `stopped_message_generation` updates were dropped by `_enqueue_update()`
  because they carry no `message`/`callback_query` payload, so the live-draft
  Stop button did nothing. They now enqueue under the draft chat id and cancel
  the matching run (regression test covers the queue path).
* Drafts address the private chat with an integer id, and session/handoff cards
  keep their ❓ / 🤝 badges instead of falling back to 🔔.

### Telegram UX: coloured buttons, emoji grammar and live run drafts

* New `perun/telegram_format.py`: one visual grammar for every message — an emoji
  badge plus a bold title, underline/strikethrough/spoiler, `>` blockquotes,
  live `<tg-time>` timestamps, plain-text stripping, and a fence-aware chunker
  that never splits a code block.
* Inline buttons now use Telegram's `style` (green = safe/affirmative, blue =
  neutral, red = destructive) and a clearer permission layout. An older Bot API
  server degrades to uncoloured buttons instead of losing them.
* A rejected HTML message is retried as plain text **with the keyboard kept**;
  the markup is dropped only when the markup itself is invalid.
* The bridge publishes its command menu with `setMyCommands`, and `/status`,
  `/health`, `/now`, `/help` and `/pending` follow the shared badge grammar.
* Digest cards prefix each item with its kind badge and add a one-tap
  **Mute project** button; `/pending` shows the same badges and timestamps.
* Private chats stream a live `sendMessageDraft` preview (tool + partial output)
  while a run generates; the draft's Stop button cancels that exact run. Groups
  keep the typing indicator.

### Proposal peek shows the changeset operations

* Clicking a `prop_…` chip in PerunChat still opens the proposal peek; the peek
  now lists each `create`/`edit`/`delete` operation with its path (instead of
  only the derived target list). Legacy rows without operations keep the
  Targets fallback.

### Non-blocking changeset hardening

* Legacy HITL token migration is now **strict**: a pre-v0.12 token is refreshed
  only when its legacy `action_type`+`targets` signature verifies. A tampered
  signature fails both payloads and is refused.
* `targets` and `action_type` are derived from `operations` when a proposal is
  read, so the UI/summary cannot disagree with the guard/package changeset even
  if the legacy columns are edited directly.
* Pending/approved legacy `other` rows are marked `failed` during migration with
  an explicit “re-propose with create/edit/delete operations” reason.
* Local-run completion now compares **content hashes** per target: an identical
  write is a real no-op (`NO TARGET CHANGES`), and a content change with a
  restored mtime is still detected.
* `derive_package()` refuses more than 100 operations defensively.
* Added a source-level UI test for the per-operation proposal chips.

### Existing approved proposals survive the changeset migration

* A HITL approval token issued before v0.12 was bound to `action_type` +
  `targets`. The changeset payload now binds `operations`, so an old token would
  have failed on claim/run and stranded a human approval. `claim_execution()` and
  `_prepare_execution()` now refresh the token from the **stored approval**
  (status, approver, seven-day window) when the signature no longer matches, and
  bind the fresh token to the current changeset. A legacy-token test covers the
  claim path.

### Guard fails closed for an executing proposal with no operations

* A legacy/invalid `executing` row whose `operations` list is empty now makes
  the guard target scope ambiguous instead of returning an empty scope. Writes
  are refused rather than silently allowed anywhere in the project allowlist.
  This can only happen for a pre-v0.12 `other` row or a corrupt row; typed
  changesets always carry operations.

### Breaking: proposals are typed changesets

* A proposal now carries **`operations`**, one `{path, op}` entry per target
  (`create`/`edit`/`delete`). One proposal can mix all three and is applied as a
  single atomic changeset, so a change that adds a file and edits another no
  longer needs a proposal chain. `action_type` is only a derived summary
  (`mixed` when the operations differ).
* `create()`/the REST envelope/the `perun-proposals_propose` MCP tool now require
  `operations`; the old `action_type` + `targets` input is removed. Existing DB
  rows are migrated once from their typed fields; `other` rows become invalid.
* `_assert_action_targets()`, `derive_package()`, the guard, the local prompt and
  the post-run check all use each target’s own operation. `guard_delete_file`
  requires a `delete` operation on that exact target; write/edit are refused for
  a delete target. A package containing a delete remains operator-only.
* The Shared-tab proposal row renders per-operation chips (`create path`,
  `edit path`, `delete path`) and shows `mixed` when the changeset differs.
* Tests cover mixed create+edit, mixed create+delete, mixed local execution,
  duplicate/invalid operations, legacy-row migration, and the existing package
  approval/rollback paths.
